podcast.title: Brief Red Hot Chili Peppers Drummer (1988)
podcast.body: D.H. Peligro was briefly hired as the new drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers in 1988 after Jack Irons quit. He was a friend of John Frusciante and connected him to the band, but ultimately "didn't work out" as the drummer. "D.H. Polegrum, the dead Kennedays, was briefly hired as a new drummer... But he didn't work out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

podcast.title: Death from Accidental Fall
podcast.body: D.H. Peligro died on October 28th, 2022, at his home in Los Angeles at 63 years old, apparently from an accidental fall in the bathroom where he struck his head, resulting in fatal trauma. "On October 28th, 2022, Pellegros died in his home in Los Angeles. He apparently had an accidental fall in the bathroom and struck his head, resulting in fatal trauma. He was 63 years old."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Versatile Drumming Style
podcast.body: Throughout the rest of his life, D.H. Peligro played in a long list of bands, banging out diverse rhythms spanning rock, reggae, and funk. "Pellegros played in a long list of bands for the rest of his life, banging out rock rhythms as well as reggae and funk."

xref.title: Continued Friendship and Support
xref.body: Despite his firing, D.H. Peligro remained friends with the Red Hot Chili Peppers, and Anthony Kiedis played a significant role in helping him achieve sobriety. "Still, everyone remained friends and Kitas was a big part in helping Pellegros get sober."

xref.title: D.H. Peligro's Brief Drummer Stint
xref.body: D.H. Peligro briefly joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers as drummer in 1988, stepping in after Jack Irons could no longer handle being a Chili Pepper following the heroin overdose death of guitarist Hillel Slovak. "In 1988 he briefly became the drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers after Jack Irons couldn't handle being a chili pepper anymore, following the heroin overdose death of guitarist Hila Slovak."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: D.H. Peligro's Tenure
xref.body: D.H. Peligro became the second drummer for the Dead Kennedys in 1981, playing on their major albums before the band broke up in 1986. "In 1991 he became the second drummer for the Dead Kennedys, one of the foundational bands on the American Hardcore scene. He was with them all through their big albums before they broke up in 1986."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Firing Due to Addiction and Replacement
xref.body: Unfortunately, D.H. Peligro's struggles with drug and alcohol demons led to his firing later in 1988, which then paved the way for Chad Smith to join the group as drummer. "Unfortunately Pellegros had his own drug and alcohol demons and was fired later the same year, paving the way for Chad Smith to join the group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
